record.paper_title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Topology Meets Functional Analysis
record.context_brief: Global hyperbolicity versus self-adjointness in non-stationary spacetimes
record.original_question: For a general non-stationary globally hyperbolic spacetime, after conformally rewriting the metric in the form g̃ = -dt² + g̃Σ,ij(t,x) dxi dxj, does global hyperbolicity impose enough geodesic-completeness structure on each spatial slice (Σ_t, g̃Σ_t) to imply essential self-adjointness of the spatial Klein-Gordon or Laplace-type operator L(t)? Equivalently, outside the static, warped-product, and uniformly controlled sliced-space settings already understood in the paper, what precise relation remains between global hyperbolicity of the Lorentzian spacetime and geodesic completeness of the associated Riemannian hypersurfaces?

evidence.quote: In the case of non-stationary spacetimes, however, the connection between global hyperbolicity and self-adjointness of the spatial Laplacian is still unclear.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, time-oriented, globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold of dimension $n+1$. By choosing a Cauchy temporal function and performing a conformal rescaling, one may write the metric in the form
$$\tilde g \;=\; -dt^{2} + \tilde g_{\Sigma,ij}(t,x)\, dx^{i}dx^{j}, \qquad t\in\mathbb{R},$$
where for each $t\in\mathbb{R}$ the slice $(\Sigma_{t},\tilde g_{\Sigma_{t}})$ is a smooth Riemannian $n$-manifold (with $\Sigma_{t}$ diffeomorphic to a fixed smooth manifold $\Sigma$). For each $t$, let $L(t)$ denote the spatial Klein–Gordon-type operator
$$L(t) \;=\; -\Delta_{\tilde g_{\Sigma_{t}}} + V(t,\cdot),$$
acting on $C_{c}^{\infty}(\Sigma_{t})\subset L^{2}(\Sigma_{t},\mathrm{vol}_{\tilde g_{\Sigma_{t}}})$, with $V$ smooth and (say) bounded below.

Assume one is outside the three already-understood settings:
(i) static spacetimes, (ii) standard warped products $\tilde g = -dt^{2} + f(t)^{2}h(x)$ with $h$ a fixed Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and (iii) sliced spaces with uniformly controlled families $\{\tilde g_{\Sigma_{t}}\}_{t}$ (e.g., uniformly equivalent to a fixed complete metric with uniform curvature/derivative bounds).

Question. In this general non-stationary regime, does global hyperbolicity of $(M,g)$ imply that each spatial slice $(\Sigma_{t},\tilde g_{\Sigma_{t}})$ is geodesically complete, and does it imply that $L(t)$ is essentially self-adjoint on $C_{c}^{\infty}(\Sigma_{t})$ for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$? More precisely, determine the exact relationship — in the absence of stationarity, warped-product structure, or uniform slice control — between global hyperbolicity of the Lorentzian manifold $(M,g)$ and geodesic completeness of the Riemannian hypersurfaces $(\Sigma_{t},\tilde g_{\Sigma_{t}})$, and characterize when essential self-adjointness of $L(t)$ follows.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (notably the 2024/2025 paper "Global Hyperbolicity and Self-adjointness," J. Geom. Phys., 2025) extends essential self-adjointness results to additional classes of globally hyperbolic spacetimes via geodesic completeness of Cauchy slices, but only for "various classes" and not for fully general non-stationary spacetimes. The general relation between global hyperbolicity and geodesic completeness of arbitrary Cauchy slices is known to fail in general, and the corresponding self-adjointness question outside the controlled settings remains open.

status_evidence.title: Global Hyperbolicity and Self-adjointness (arXiv:2410.04879)
status_evidence.snippet: The spatial part of the Klein-Gordon operator is essentially self-adjoint on Cauchy surfaces of various classes of spacetimes, using connections between global hyperbolicity and geodesic completeness.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves the question only for specific classes, not for fully general non-stationary spacetimes.

status_evidence.title: Self-Adjointness in Klein-Gordon Theory on Globally Hyperbolic Spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: Essential self-adjointness proven assuming smoothness and semi-boundedness for static and stationary spacetimes; generalization to time-dependent metrics indicated as nontrivial.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms that the non-stationary general case is not settled and requires additional structure (complex structure construction is involved).

status_evidence.title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Some Recent Advances and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey lists open problems concerning the connection between global hyperbolicity and geodesic completeness/self-adjointness in non-stationary settings.
status_evidence.claim: Listed among open problems in recent surveys.
